notes.title: Stories about weather
notes.science: People tell stories to explain forces they cannot see, and they give those forces faces and moods.
notes.limits: This myth is built from what you did, chosen by a few rules. It is not a reading of your heart.
notes.counter: Some say a myth hides as much as it shows.
notes.question: Did the story sound like you?

sources.label: On Seeing Human, Epley, Waytz and Cacioppo, 2007
An Experimental Study of Apparent Behavior, Heider and Simmel, 1944

notes.title: Being seen
notes.science: Hearing how others saw you can change what you do next. Kith tells you what it remembers.
notes.limits: The creatures only tell what the sim recorded.
notes.counter: We often judge others by their acts and ourselves by our intentions, so their story and yours can both be fair.
notes.question: What would you do again?

sources.label: The Intuitive Psychologist and His Shortcomings, Ross, 1977
The Evolution of Trust, Nicky Case
